mainTopic: Lessons from אברהם's hospitality, the miracles of יצחק's birth, and workers' meals and their right to eat
overview: The גמרא continues reading the פסוקים about אברהם's guests and draws lessons from small details: you should not turn down a great person, צדיקים say little and do much while רשעים like עפרון do the opposite, and a woman tends to be more sparing with guests. It explains that the bread was never served because שרה became a נדה, and that the guests asked 'where is שרה' to show her modesty or to send her the כוס של ברכה. From this the גמרא learns that a guest may ask about a woman through her husband. It also teaches that peace is so great that הקב״ה changed שרה's words, and it tells how miracles at יצחק's weaning feast proved he was truly the son of אברהם and שרה. Next comes a list of firsts: visible old age with אברהם, illness before death with יעקב, and recovery from illness with אלישע. The גמרא then returns to the earlier משנה about feeding workers. It confirms the wording 'bread and legumes' and shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word 'everything' includes paying a worker by the local wage. Finally, a new משנה begins listing which workers may eat from the produce by Torah law, and the list of those who may not eat continues on the next amud.

steps.title: You may turn down a lesser person but not a great person
steps.stepSummary: From the fact that לוט had to press the מלאכים hard before they agreed, רבי אלעזר learns that one may decline a lesser person's invitation but not a great person's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק say לוט "urged them greatly"? רבי אלעזר says: this teaches that you may refuse a lesser person, but you may not refuse a great person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why לוט had to beg the מלאכים so hard, and רבי אלעזר draws a rule of manners from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With אברהם, the guests agreed right away. With לוט, they first said no and only gave in after he pushed. רבי אלעזר explains the difference: it is fine to turn down someone less important, but you should not turn down an invitation from a great person like אברהם.

phrases.english: "And he urged them greatly"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 19:3. The מלאכים first said no to לוט, but they agreed to אברהם right away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: From here we learn
that one may decline a lesser person,
but one may not decline a great person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּפְצַר בָּם מְאֹד? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִכָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the מלאכים' visits to אברהם and לוט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may decline the request of a lesser person, but not the request of a great person.

steps.title: The righteous say little and do much
steps.stepSummary: אברהם promised only a bit of bread but then ran to bring a whole calf, so רבי אלעזר learns that צדיקים say little and do much, while רשעים say much and do nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says אברהם offered "a piece of bread," and another says he ran to the cattle. רבי אלעזר says: this teaches that צדיקים say little and do a lot, but רשעים say a lot and don't do even a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two פסוקים side by side, a small promise and a big action, and רבי אלעזר learns a lesson about character.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם's words were modest (just bread), but his actions were generous (a whole tender calf). רבי אלעזר turns this into a general rule and adds the opposite rule for רשעים, which the גמרא will prove in the next step.

phrases.english: It is written: "And I will fetch a morsel of bread,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:5

phrases.english: and it is written: "And Abraham ran to the herd,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:7

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: From here we learn
that the righteous say little and do much,
the wicked say much,
and do not do even a little.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב: וְאֶקְחָה פַת לֶחֶם, וּכְתִיב: וְאֶל הַבָּקָר רָץ אַבְרָהָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another lesson from the same story of אברהם's guests.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים say little and do much; רשעים say much and do not do even a little.

steps.title: Proof from עפרון that the wicked say much and do little
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the second half of רבי אלעזר's rule and brings עפרון, who talked as if the land was nearly free but ended up taking the full price in heavy, high-value coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this about רשעים? From עפרון. At first he said, "land worth four hundred shekels, what is that between us?" But in the end אברהם paid him four hundred shekels of silver "accepted by merchants" — meaning עפרון took only big, valuable coins, since in some places a shekel is called a kantera.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we see that רשעים promise a lot and give nothing, and answers by showing what עפרון said versus what he actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עפרון's words made it sound like he did not care about money at all. Yet he took the full four hundred shekels, and the words "current with the merchant" show he insisted on the best, heaviest coins. So he spoke generously but acted greedily, exactly the pattern of רשעים.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?

steps.whatToRemember: צדיקים like אברהם promise little and give a lot; רשעים like עפרון promise a lot and give nothing.

phrases.english: From where do we know this? From Ephron.
phrases.notes: He means the second half of the rule, that the wicked say much and do nothing.

phrases.english: At first it is written:
"A land of four hundred shekels of silver,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 23:15. The פסוק goes on: "what is that between me and you?"

phrases.english: and in the end it is written:
"And Abraham listened to Ephron,
and Abraham weighed out to Ephron the silver
which he had named in the hearing of the children of Heth,

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף עֹבֵר לַסֹּחֵר״,
phrases.english: four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant."
phrases.notes: בראשית 23:16

phrases.english: meaning he took from him only centenaria (large, valuable coins),
for there is a place
where they call a shekel a "kantera."

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן, מֵעֶפְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a source for the second half of רבי אלעזר's statement in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רשעים say much and do not do even a little.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between עפרון's generous-sounding words (בראשית 23:15) and his taking the full price in high-value coins (בראשית 23:16).

steps.title: Flour and fine flour: a woman is more careful with guests
steps.stepSummary: Because the פסוק says both "flour" and "fine flour," רבי יצחק learns that a woman is more sparing with guests than a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "flour" and also "fine flour." רבי יצחק says: this teaches that a woman is more sparing toward guests than a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that one פסוק uses two words for the flour, and רבי יצחק explains why both are there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double wording suggests two opinions about what to serve: plain flour or fine flour. רבי יצחק reads it as שרה leaning toward the cheaper flour and אברהם toward the finer one. From this he learns that a woman tends to be more careful about spending on guests.

keyTerms.meaning: she is stingy / sparing (literally, her eye is narrow)

phrases.english: It is written "flour," and it is written "fine flour."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:6. Both words appear together in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: From here we learn
that a woman is stingy with guests
more than a man.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב קֶמַח וּכְתִיב סֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another lesson drawn from the same story of אברהם hosting his guests.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman is more sparing with guests than a man, learned from the double wording קמח and סולת.

steps.title: Why was the bread never served?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that אברהם told שרה to bake cakes, but the next פסוקים list only curd, milk and meat. The bread is missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'Knead and make cakes,' and it also says 'He took curd, milk and the calf.' But bread he did not bring them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a gap between two פסוקים. Bread was prepared, but it is never served. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם ordered cakes in פסוק ו, but in פסוק ח, when he actually serves the guests, the list has no bread. Something must have stopped the bread from reaching the table, and the גמרא wants to know what.

phrases.english: It is written: "Knead and make cakes,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:6

phrases.english: and it is written: "And he took curd and milk
and the calf,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:8

phrases.english: and yet bread he did not bring before them!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב ״לוּשִׁי וַעֲשִׂי עֻגוֹת״, וּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same story of אברהם's guests and raises a new difficulty in the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bread was prepared but not served. The פסוקים seem not to fit together.

steps.title: שרה became a נדה, so the bread was impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that אברהם ate even ordinary food in purity, and שרה became a נדה that day, which made the dough impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: אפרים מקשאה, רבי מאיר's student, said in רבי מאיר's name: אברהם ate ordinary food in purity, and that day שרה became a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question of the missing bread. The dough שרה made became טמא, so אברהם would not serve it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם kept the standards of purity even for ordinary food, חולין. When שרה became a נדה, the dough she had handled became impure. Since אברהם only served food that was טהור, the bread was left off the table.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy food eaten with the care of purity
She began her monthly period and became a נדה

phrases.english: Efrayim Miksha'a said,
the student of Rabbi Meir,
in the name of Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ אוֹכֵל חוּלִּין בְּטׇהֳרָה הָיָה,
phrases.english: Avraham our father would eat ordinary food in purity,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׂרָה אִמֵּנוּ אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם פֵּירְסָה נִדָּה.
phrases.english: and Sarah our mother became a niddah that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶפְרַיִם מִקְשָׁאָה תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the missing bread.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bread was prepared but forgotten or skipped for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bread became טמא because שרה became a נדה, and אברהם ate only pure food.
steps.whatToRemember: The bread was missing because שרה became a נדה that day, and אברהם ate even חולין in purity.

steps.title: 'Where is שרה?' shows her modesty
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק records the guests asking where שרה was and אברהם answering 'in the tent.' This teaches that שרה was modest.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They said to him: Where is Sarah your wife? He said: Here, in the tent.' This teaches that שרה was modest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and explains its message. שרה stayed inside while guests were there, which shows her modesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have skipped this short exchange. It is included to praise שרה, who stayed in the tent and did not come out among the men.

phrases.english: "And they said to him: Where is Sarah your wife?
And he said: Here, in the tent,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:9

phrases.english: to let us know that Sarah our mother was modest.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו אַיֵּה שָׂרָה אִשְׁתֶּךָ וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה בָאֹהֶל״, לְהוֹדִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק teaches that שרה was modest.

steps.title: The מלאכים asked to make שרה more beloved to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רב, or רבי יצחק, says the מלאכים already knew שרה was in the tent. They asked so that אברהם's answer would show her modesty and make her more dear to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say רבי יצחק: The מלאכים knew שרה was in the tent. So why ask? To make her more beloved to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: This explains why the מלאכים asked a question they already knew the answer to. Their purpose was to make שרה more beloved to אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלאכים did not need information, so the question must have had another purpose. By getting אברהם to say 'she is in the tent,' they made him notice her modesty, and that drew him closer to her.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yitzchak:
The ministering angels knew
that Sarah our mother was in the tent;
rather, what is the point of "in the tent"?
In order to make her beloved to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹדְעִים הָיוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת שֶׁשָּׂרָה אִמֵּנוּ בָּאֹהֶל הָיְתָה, אֶלָּא מַאי ״בָּאֹהֶל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the מלאכים asked at all, building on the modesty point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאכים asked in order to make שרה more beloved to אברהם.

steps.title: They asked in order to send her the כוס של ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives a different reason for the question: the guests wanted to send שרה the cup of wine used for the blessing after the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: They asked in order to send her the כוס של ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second explanation of why the מלאכים asked where שרה was. They wanted to send her the cup of blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question has a practical purpose. After the meal, the guests wanted שרה to get a share of the כוס של ברכה, so they asked where she was in order to send it to her.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup of wine over which ברכת המזון is said

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְשַׁגֵּר לָהּ כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה.
phrases.english: In order to send her the cup of blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: כְּדֵי לְשַׁגֵּר לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason than step 8 for why the מלאכים asked about שרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאכים asked so they could send שרה the כוס של ברכה.

steps.title: The dots on אליו teach good manners
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יוסי says the dots over א-י-ו in אליו spell 'where is he?' This teaches that a guest should ask the hostess about her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in רבי יוסי's name: Why are the letters א-י-ו in אליו dotted? The Torah is teaching manners: a person should ask his hostess about the host.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the dots written over the word אליו in the ספר תורה. They teach a lesson in דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dotted letters spell אַיּוֹ, 'where is he?' This hints that the מלאכים also asked שרה where אברהם was. Just as you ask the host about his wife, you should ask the hostess about her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Dotted, marked with dots above the letters

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
Why are there dots on the alef-yod-vav of "to him"?
phrases.notes: Those three dotted letters spell אַיּוֹ, which means "where is he?"

phrases.english: The Torah taught proper manners,
that a person should ask of his hostess.
phrases.notes: He means: a guest should ask the woman of the house how her husband is doing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לָמָּה נָקוּד עַל אַיּוֹ שֶׁבְּ״אֵלָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further lesson from the same word אליו in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guest should ask the hostess about the host, just as he asks the host about her.

steps.title: שמואל says not to greet a woman at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with שמואל's rule that one may not ask about a woman's welfare at all. So how could the מלאכים ask about שרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't שמואל say: You may not ask about a woman's welfare at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge from שמואל's rule. It seems to clash with the מלאכים asking about שרה, and with the manners just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל forbids asking about a woman's welfare for reasons of modesty. Yet the story shows the מלאכים asking about שרה, and the Torah presents it as proper behavior. These two seem to contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? This opens a challenge

phrases.english: But didn't Shmuel say:
One may not ask about a woman's welfare at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין שׁוֹאֲלִין בִּשְׁלוֹם אִשָּׁה כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea that asking about the woman of the house is proper.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מלאכים asking אברהם about שרה, presented as proper manners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל forbids asking about a woman's welfare at all, so the behavior in the story seems improper.

steps.title: Asking through her husband is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that asking about a woman through her husband is different and is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through her husband, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers שמואל's challenge. The מלאכים asked אברהם about שרה, and asking through the husband is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule is about asking a woman directly, or asking about her in a way that is not modest. Asking her husband how his wife is doing does not raise that concern, so the story fits the rule.

phrases.english: Through her husband, it is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל יְדֵי בַּעְלָהּ שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (an exception)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any asking about a woman's welfare is forbidden, even through her husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's rule does not cover asking through the husband, which is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל forbids asking about a woman's welfare, but asking her husband about her is fine, just as the מלאכים asked אברהם about שרה.

steps.title: שרה's youth and beauty return
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains the words 'אחרי בלתי היתה לי עדנה': שרה's worn, wrinkled skin became smooth again, and her beauty returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'After I am worn out, shall I have smoothness?' רב חסדא says: after her skin had worn out and become full of wrinkles, it became soft again, the wrinkles smoothed out, and her beauty came back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שרה's words from the פסוק, and רב חסדא explains what the word עדנה means here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא reads עדנה as the skin becoming soft and smooth, not just as 'pleasure.' So שרה is describing a real physical change: her body became young again. This sets up that a miracle was already starting before יצחק was born.

phrases.english: "After I am worn out, shall I have smoothness?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:12

phrases.english: Rav Chisda says:
After the skin had worn out
and the wrinkles had multiplied,
the skin became soft again
and the wrinkles smoothed out,
and the beauty returned to its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבַּלָּה הַבָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the מלאכים's question about שרה to explaining שרה's own words in the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדנה means שרה's skin became smooth again and her beauty returned.

steps.title: הקב״ה did not repeat שרה's exact words
steps.stepSummary: שרה said 'my lord is old,' but when הקב״ה repeated her words to אברהם, He said 'and I am old.' He changed what she said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written that שרה said 'and my lord is old,' and it is written that הקב״ה told אברהם she said 'and I am old.' So הקב״ה did not repeat what she actually said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a difference between two פסוקים. This sets up the question of why הקב״ה changed שרה's words, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, שרה says her husband is old. In the next פסוק, הקב״ה reports her as saying that she herself is old. The גמרא notices that the report does not match the original, which needs an explanation.

phrases.english: It is written: "And my lord is old,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:12. Here שרה is talking about אברהם.

phrases.english: and it is written: "And I am old"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:13

phrases.english: for the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not repeat
what she herself had said.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב ״וַאדֹנִי זָקֵן״, וּכְתִיב ״וַאֲנִי זָקַנְתִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the same פסוק about שרה's laughter, now comparing it to how הקב״ה quoted her.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way הקב״ה reported שרה's words to אברהם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים describe the same statement differently. Why would הקב״ה not repeat her words accurately?

steps.title: Peace is so great that הקב״ה changed the words
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that peace is so important that even הקב״ה changed the truth for it. He did not tell אברהם that שרה called him old.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Peace is great, since even הקב״ה changed the facts for it. As it says: 'And שרה laughed within herself... and my lord is old,' and it is written: 'And ה׳ said to אברהם... and I am old.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains why הקב״ה changed שרה's words: to keep peace between her and אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אברהם had heard that שרה called him old, it could have hurt their relationship. So הקב״ה reported it as if she spoke about herself. This shows that keeping peace can be worth changing the exact wording.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
and so on (the rest of the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: שלום בית is so important that even הקב״ה changed שרה's words so that אברהם would not be hurt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source that one may change the facts for the sake of peace.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Peace is great,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שִׁינָּה בּוֹ,
phrases.english: for even the Holy One, Blessed be He, changed the facts for it,
as it is said: "And Sarah laughed within herself
etc., and my lord is old,"
and it is written: "And the Lord said to Abraham
etc., and I am old."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: גָּדוֹל שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the difference raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason (value-based explanation) for the change in wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed strange that הקב״ה would not report שרה's words exactly.
steps.terutzMaskana: He changed them on purpose to keep peace between שרה and אברהם.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say שרה nursed 'children'?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says שרה nursed 'children' in the plural. The גמרא asks how many children she nursed, since she had only יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And she said: Who would have told אברהם that שרה would nurse children?' How many children did שרה nurse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק and asks a question about one word in it. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרה gave birth only to יצחק, yet the פסוק uses the plural 'children.' The גמרא wants to know what the plural is teaching.

phrases.english: "And she said: Who would have said to Abraham
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:7

phrases.english: that Sarah would nurse children?"
How many children did Sarah nurse?

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה בָּנִים הֵנִיקָה שָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a later פסוק, after יצחק's birth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק says 'children' when שרה had only one child.

steps.title: The weaning feast and the nations' gossip
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי begins his answer. At יצחק's weaning feast, the nations gossiped that אברהם and שרה had found a baby in the market and were claiming he was theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי says: On the day אברהם weaned his son יצחק, he made a big feast. All the nations of the world were gossiping and saying: 'Have you seen this old man and old woman? They brought a foundling from the market and say: He is our son! And on top of that, they are making a big feast to make their claim believable!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי starts answering the question by telling the story of the weaning feast. Here he only sets the scene with the nations' gossip, and the next step gives the answer itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nations did not believe that such an old couple could have a child. They thought the feast was a show to convince people that the baby was really theirs. This doubt sets up how the plural 'children' will be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: a foundling, an abandoned baby picked up

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished here. The next step continues the story and explains the plural 'children.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi says:
On that day when Abraham weaned
his son Isaac,
he made a great feast.
All the nations of the world were
gossiping and saying:
Have you seen this old man and old woman
who brought a foundling from the market
and are saying: He is our son!
And not only that, but
they are making a great feast
to back up their claim!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שֶׁגָּמַל אַבְרָהָם אֶת יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial so far: it sets the scene of the weaning feast and the nations' doubt that יצחק was really אברהם and שרה's son. The explanation of 'children' continues next.

steps.title: Sarah nurses all the guests' babies
steps.stepSummary: אברהם and שרה invited the great people of the generation and their wives. A miracle let שרה nurse all their babies. This proved she was really יצחק's mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did אברהם do? He invited all the great men of the generation, and שרה invited their wives. Each woman brought her baby but not her wet nurse. A miracle happened, and שרה had milk like two springs. She nursed all the babies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבי לוי's answer from the last step. It tells how אברהם and שרה proved that יצחק was really their son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nations said אברהם and שרה found a baby in the market. If שרה could nurse many babies, she must have truly given birth herself. This also answers the question from step 16: the פסוק says 'children' in the plural because שרה nursed the guests' children too.

keyTerms.meaning: the great people of the generation
a wet nurse, a woman who nurses another woman's baby

steps.whatToRemember: The 'children' שרה nursed were the guests' babies. Her nursing them proved she was יצחק's real mother.

phrases.english: What did אברהם our father do?
He went and invited all the great men of the generation,
and שרה our mother invited their wives.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אַחַת וְאַחַת הֵבִיאָה בְּנָהּ עִמָּהּ,
phrases.english: Each and every one brought her child with her,
but she did not bring her wet nurse,
and a miracle happened to שרה our mother
and her breasts opened like two springs,
and she nursed all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עָשָׂה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי לוי's answer from step 17 and resolves the plural 'children' from step 16. The story goes on in step 19 with a second rumor and a second miracle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שרה nursed many children, meaning the guests' babies. This proved she gave birth to יצחק.

steps.title: יצחק's face changes to look like אברהם
steps.stepSummary: People still gossiped that a 100-year-old אברהם could not father a child. Right away יצחק's face changed to look just like אברהם, and everyone said 'אברהם fathered יצחק.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They still gossiped: 'Maybe שרה at ninety can give birth, but can אברהם at a hundred father a child?' Right away יצחק's face changed to look like אברהם's, and everyone said: 'אברהם fathered יצחק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going with a second rumor, this time about אברהם. A new miracle answers that rumor too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first miracle proved שרה was the mother, but people now doubted that אברהם was the father. When יצחק looked exactly like אברהם, nobody could doubt it. This explains the words of the פסוק 'אברהם הוליד את יצחק.'

phrases.english: And still they were gossiping and saying:
"Even if שרה, at ninety years old, can give birth,
can אברהם, at a hundred years old, father a child?"

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד נֶהְפַּךְ קְלַסְתֵּר פָּנִים שֶׁל יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Immediately the features of יצחק's face changed
and looked like אברהם's.
Everyone spoke up and said:
"אברהם fathered יצחק."
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:19

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲדַיִין הָיוּ מְרַנְּנִים וְאוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rumor and a second miracle to the same story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יצחק's face came to look like אברהם's, which proved אברהם was his father.

steps.title: אברהם prays for old age to show
steps.stepSummary: Before אברהם, people did not look old, so others confused אברהם with יצחק. אברהם prayed, and old age began to show.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until אברהם, old age did not show. Someone who wanted to talk to אברהם would talk to יצחק, and someone who wanted to talk to יצחק would talk to אברהם. אברהם prayed, and old age began to show, as the פסוק says: 'And אברהם was old, well along in days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on from the story of the feast. It starts a new teaching, connected to the idea that אברהם and יצחק looked alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since father and son looked the same, people could not tell them apart. אברהם asked for old age to be visible on the body, and the גמרא brings the פסוק 'ואברהם זקן בא בימים' as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: old age, the signs of aging
he prayed, he asked for mercy

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean people never got older before אברהם. It means age did not show on their faces and bodies.

phrases.english: Until אברהם there was no old age.
phrases.notes: He means old age didn't show on a person, so an old man looked like a young one.

phrases.english: Someone who wanted to talk with אברהם
phrases.notes: Both words mean 'to talk.' The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, and some versions leave out the one in round brackets.

phrases.english: would talk with יצחק.
Someone who wanted to talk with יצחק would talk with אברהם.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא אַבְרָהָם בְּעָא רַחֲמֵי וַהֲוָה זִקְנָה,
phrases.english: אברהם came and prayed, and there was old age,
as it says: "And אברהם was old, well along in days."
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:1

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד אַבְרָהָם לֹא הָיָה זִקְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching that builds on אברהם and יצחק looking alike
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Old age first became visible because אברהם prayed for it.

steps.title: יעקב prays for illness before death
steps.stepSummary: Before יעקב, people did not become sick before dying. יעקב prayed, and illness came into the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until יעקב there was no illness. יעקב prayed, and illness came, as the פסוק says: 'And someone said to יוסף: Behold, your father is sick.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same pattern with a second example. It shows another thing that started because one of the אבות prayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before יעקב, a person died suddenly without getting sick first. יעקב asked for an illness before death so a person could get ready. The פסוק about יעקב being sick is the first time the Torah mentions someone being sick.

phrases.english: Until יעקב there was no illness.
phrases.notes: He means illness that comes before death. Before this, people just died suddenly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא יַעֲקֹב בְּעָא רַחֲמֵי וַהֲוָה חוּלְשָׁא,
phrases.english: יעקב came and prayed, and there was illness,
as it says: "And he said to יוסף: Behold, your father is sick."
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:1

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד יַעֲקֹב לָא הֲוָה חוּלְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of the same 'until X, there was no Y' pattern
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Illness before death began because יעקב prayed for it.

steps.title: אלישע is the first to get sick and recover
steps.stepSummary: Before אלישע, anyone who got sick died. אלישע prayed and was healed. We know this because the פסוק says that his last illness was the one he would die from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until אלישע came, nobody got sick and then got better. אלישע prayed and got better, as the פסוק says: 'And אלישע fell sick with the illness from which he would die.' This shows he had been sick before with other illnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third example of the same pattern. It also explains how we can learn this from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses 'the illness from which he would die.' That only makes sense if he had other illnesses that he did not die from. So אלישע was the first person to recover from a sickness.

phrases.aramaic: עַד דַּאֲתָא אֱלִישָׁע לָא הֲוָה דְּחָלֵישׁ וְאִתְּפַח.
phrases.english: Until אלישע came, there was no one who got sick and recovered.
אלישע came and prayed, and he recovered,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וֶאֱלִישָׁע חָלָה אֶת חׇלְיוֹ אֲשֶׁר יָמוּת בּוֹ״ –
phrases.english: as it says: "And אלישע fell sick with his illness from which he would die"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 13:14

phrases.english: which shows that he had been sick with another illness.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד דַּאֲתָא אֱלִישָׁע לָא הֲוָה דְּחָלֵישׁ וְאִתְּפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third example of the pattern, with a proof drawn from the wording of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Recovery from illness began with אלישע's prayer.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists אלישע's three illnesses
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis taught that אלישע had three illnesses. One came for pushing away גיחזי with both hands, one came for sending bears against the children, and the last was the one he died from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: אלישע had three illnesses. One was because he pushed away גיחזי with both hands. One was because he set bears on the children. One was the illness he died from, as the פסוק says: 'And אלישע fell sick with the illness from which he would die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds details about אלישע's illnesses. It tells us what the earlier illnesses were and why they came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed that אלישע had illnesses before his last one. This ברייתא names them. The first two were punishments for being too harsh, and the third was the illness that ended his life.

keyTerms.meaning: he set against, he stirred up

steps.whatToRemember: There are three firsts here: אברהם prayed for old age to show, יעקב prayed for illness before death, and אלישע was the first to recover from illness. אלישע had three illnesses in all.

phrases.english: The rabbis taught:
אלישע was sick with three illnesses:
one because he pushed גיחזי away with both hands,
phrases.notes: See מלכים ב chapter 5.

phrases.english: one because he set bears against the children,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:23-25

phrases.english: and one that he died from,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וֶאֱלִישָׁע חָלָה אֶת חׇלְיוֹ אֲשֶׁר יָמוּת בּוֹ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "And אלישע fell sick with his illness from which he would die."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳלָאִין חָלָה אֱלִישָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the earlier illnesses that step 22 inferred from the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלישע had three illnesses: two came as punishment, and the third was the one he died from.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה's line about bread and legumes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the earlier משנה where רבי יוחנן בן מתיא tells his son to limit the workers to bread and legumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, before they start working, go out and tell them: 'This is on condition that all you can claim from me is bread and legumes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the earlier משנה so it can ask a question about its exact wording. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His son had promised the workers food without setting a limit, so they could demand a feast. The fix was to set a limit before the work starts: only bread and legumes, the simple meal workers usually got. The exact wording of this line is about to be questioned.

phrases.english: Rather, before they begin the work,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן בן מתיא speaking to his son in the משנה back on 83a.

phrases.english: go out and say to them:
on condition that you have no claim on me
except bread and legumes, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַתְחִילוּ בַּמְּלָאכָה צֵא וֶאֱמוֹר לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about אלישע and returns to the wording of the משנה about feeding workers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An employer can limit his promise of food by stating, before the work starts, that the workers get only bread and legumes.

steps.title: Is it 'bread of legumes' or 'bread and legumes'?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף asks רב חסדא whether the משנה says 'bread of legumes' or 'bread and legumes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב יוסף asked רב חסדא: Does our משנה say 'bread of legumes,' or 'bread and legumes'?
steps.whatsHappening: A sage asks which wording of the משנה is correct, because one small letter changes what the workers get.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the letter ו, it means a cheap bread baked from legume flour, which is only one poor item. With the ו, it means two foods: regular bread plus a side of legumes. The question is how much the employer must give.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Yosef, said to Rav Chisda:
Did we learn 'bread of legumes,'
or did we learn 'bread and legumes'?

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּת קִטְנִית תְּנַן, אוֹ פַּת וְקִטְנִית תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the exact wording of the line quoted in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה reads פת קטנית (one poor food) or פת וקטנית (bread plus legumes).

steps.title: רב חסדא: definitely 'bread and legumes'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא swears that the ו belongs there, as big as an oar, so the correct wording is 'bread and legumes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: By God! That word needs a ו as big as a cypress-wood oar.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers with great force: the correct wording is 'bread and legumes,' with the ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture of a ו 'as big as an oar' means there is no doubt at all about this letter. So the workers get two things, real bread and legumes, not just a cheap legume bread.
steps.whatToRemember: The correct wording is פת וקטנית: the workers get bread AND legumes, not just a cheap legume bread.

phrases.english: He said to him: By God!
It needs a vav
phrases.notes: He means the word קִטְנִית must start with ו, 'and.'

phrases.english: as big as an oar made of cypress wood.
phrases.notes: In other words, the ו is so clearly there that you couldn't miss it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָאֱלֹהִים צְרִיכָה וָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The correct reading is פת וקטנית, bread and legumes.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: everything follows local custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה: the son did not need to say this, because everything follows local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He did not need to say this. Everything follows the custom of the place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the earlier משנה so it can ask about one word in it. This step sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the son did not need to set a limit, because even without one, the workers only get what is normal in that place. His rule uses the word 'everything,' which the גמרא will now examine.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not need to (say it)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He did not need to say this,
phrases.notes: He means the son did not need to set a limit on the food at all.

phrases.english: everything follows the custom of the place.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers' terms follow local custom even without a stated limit.

steps.title: What does the word 'everything' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the word 'everything' is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'everything': what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the extra word 'everything' and asks what new case it is meant to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל could have just said 'it follows local custom.' The word 'everything' suggests a wider rule that covers more cases, so the גמרא looks for the extra case.

phrases.english: 'Everything' comes to include what?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines one word in the rule quoted in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which additional case is included by the word הכל.

steps.title: It includes paying a worker 'like the townspeople'
steps.stepSummary: 'Everything' includes a case where a worker is hired 'like one or two of the townspeople.' רבי יהושע says he gets the lowest wage, and חכמים say he gets the average.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes what we learned: If someone hires a worker and tells him, 'You'll be paid like one or two of the townspeople,' he pays him the lowest wage. This is the view of רבי יהושע. חכמים say: you take the average between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everything' adds a case about wages: what to pay when the boss said only 'like the other workers in town.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wages in town differ, so 'like one or two of the townspeople' is unclear. רבי יהושע says the worker gets only the lowest wage. חכמים say he gets the average between the high and low wages, and this too is following local custom.

keyTerms.meaning: they take the average between them

steps.whatToRemember: The word הכל in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule includes the case of hiring 'like the townspeople': רבי יהושע says lowest wage, חכמים say the average.

phrases.english: It includes what we learned:
One who hires a worker and said to him:
'like one or two of the townspeople'
gives him the lowest of the wages,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.
And the Sages say: they take the average between them.
phrases.notes: Literally 'they make it fat between them': you find the middle point between the highest and lowest wages.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes the case of a worker hired at the townspeople's rate, which is set by local wage practice.

steps.title: New משנה: workers who may eat by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists which workers may eat from the produce by Torah law: someone harvesting attached produce, someone working detached produce before its processing is finished, and only with things that grow from the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These may eat by Torah law: one who works with produce attached to the ground at the time its work is finished; one who works with produce detached from the ground before its work is finished; and only with things that grow from the land.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which workers have a Torah right to eat from the food they are working with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of permitted workers. One is still in the field, at the final stage like harvesting. The other works with already-picked produce that is not yet fully processed. Both apply only to produce that grows from the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: the finishing stage of the work

steps.confusionAlert: The timing is opposite in the two cases. For attached produce, eating is allowed at the END of the work, like harvesting. For detached produce, eating is allowed only BEFORE the work is finished.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these may eat by Torah law:
one who works with produce attached to the ground
at the time the work is being finished,
and with produce detached from the ground
before its work is finished,
and with something that grows from the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵלּוּ אוֹכְלִין מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: the worker's right to eat from the produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worker may eat by Torah law when he harvests attached produce at the end of its work, or works with detached produce before its work is done, as long as it grows from the land.

steps.title: משנה begins the list of workers who may not eat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing workers who may not eat, starting with one who works with produce attached to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these may not eat: one who works with produce attached to the ground...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the opposite list, workers who may not eat. The sentence continues on the next page.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the last step. Work on attached produce gives no right to eat if it is not at the finishing stage, and the details come in the rest of the sentence.

phrases.english: And these may not eat:
one who works with produce attached to the ground
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. It goes on to say 'not at the time the work is being finished.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין אוֹכְלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the list of workers who may not eat, the opposite of step 30's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some workers with attached produce may not eat, and the details continue in the משנה.
